correctness.rationale: The 30-vertex Laplacian has eigenvalue multiplicities 1,9,10,9,1, obtained from BB^T=4I+J-T^TT and TT^T=4I+J_6. The 10-dimensional eigenvalue-3 space forces 5 selected edge vertices and 5 selected matching vertices; their two rank-ten incidence conditions are exactly PBH. Eigenvalues 1 and 5 reduce to the same 10-by-9 integer restriction rank. A standalone no-dependency verifier exhausts 3003 choices on each side, 720 label automorphisms, eight complete point orbits and every 1518 admissible matching partner per orbit. Hadamard bounds 243 and 10077696 are both below the chosen prime 1000000007, so every rank test is exact over Q. It finds exactly 36 star–spread failures and 2304288 successes, and cross-checks 30-state reachability for positive and negative examples. Only the finite stated graph is claimed.

evidence: Zhang–Camlibel–Cao 2011, Sec. V Theorems 1 and 2: for distance-regular order n and diameter d, d*m >= n-1 is necessary; n-d leaders suffice by a construction. For the graph here n=30,d=4, yielding m>=8 and a 26-leader construction, not the exact ten-coordinate placement classification.
Burgarth et al. arXiv:1111.1475, Sec. 1 and principal controllability theorem: zero forcing is a sufficient condition, with no necessity for this particular unit Laplacian.
Yuan et al. 2013 covers the spectral multiplicity lower-bound principle, not the enumerative exceptional-pair theorem.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The most relevant full-text general theories leave a strict gap between spectral bounds and all coordinate placements. A numerical lower or upper bound cannot imply 2,304,288 admissible placements out of 15-choose-5 squared nor their 36 geometric exceptions.

value.rationale: The graph is the canonical smallest thick generalized-quadrangle incidence network, giving a mathematically natural finite benchmark. Knowing all 2304288 minimum coordinate-actuator placements, not merely a lower bound, makes the result usable for exact design and reveals an exceptional rank obstruction (all 6x6 ovoid–spread pairs) that survives separate restrictions from the largest eigenspace. This is a complete sharply bounded classification rather than an arbitrary parameter slice; no downstream all-order claim is needed for the exact finite invariant to have value.
